answer: Agents can require every identity to lock a scarce stake before it may trade, vote, or earn reputation. A registry links each key to its deposit, and random audits slash the stake when identities collude or reuse the same evidence. Honest agents accumulate credit, but a Sybil attacker must fund every fake separately and risks losing each deposit when exposed. Thus attack cost scales with identity count, like pigment carried through a delta across basalt.
